services.name: DiagTrack
services.description: Collects and transmits diagnostic and usage telemetry data to Microsoft in the background.
services.impact: None for normal use. Stops continuous background telemetry reporting and disk/network activity.

services.name: dmwappushservice
services.displayName: Device Management Wireless Application Protocol (WAP) Push
services.description: Routes WAP Push messages and assists in telemetry collection and device management.
services.impact: None for home and gaming PCs.

services.name: WerSvc
services.description: Logs and sends crash dumps and error reports to Microsoft when applications hang or crash.
services.impact: Removes the 'Checking for a solution to the problem...' dialog when apps crash.

services.name: dps
services.description: Enables problem detection, troubleshooting, and resolution for Windows components.
services.impact: Built-in Windows Troubleshooters (e.g., Network Troubleshooter) will not function while disabled.

services.name: WdiServiceHost
services.description: Hosts diagnostic services used by the Diagnostic Policy Service to inspect system events.
services.impact: Windows automatic troubleshooters won't run background diagnostics.

services.name: WdiSystemHost
services.description: Hosts system-level diagnostic drivers and checks.
services.impact: Windows automatic troubleshooters won't run background diagnostics.

services.name: PcaSvc
services.description: Monitors programs installed and run by the user for known legacy compatibility issues.
services.impact: None unless you frequently run 20-year-old Windows XP installers.

services.name: MapsBroker
services.description: Background daemon that manages offline maps for the built-in Windows Maps app.
services.impact: Offline maps in the Windows Maps app will not auto-update.

services.name: RetailDemo
services.description: Used by retail stores (like Best Buy) to put PCs into a store display loop.
services.impact: Zero impact. Completely useless on personal computers.

services.name: Fax
services.description: Enables sending and receiving faxes via an analog phone modem.
services.impact: None unless you have a physical 1990s phone line fax modem connected.

services.name: RemoteRegistry
services.description: Allows remote network users to modify registry settings on your computer.
services.impact: Improves security. No impact for non-enterprise personal PCs.

services.name: wisvc
services.description: Manages beta builds for users enrolled in the Windows Insider Program.
services.impact: Do not disable only if you actively install experimental Windows Insider preview builds.

services.name: WalletService
services.description: Legacy service used by the deprecated Microsoft Wallet app.
services.impact: Zero impact.

services.name: PhoneSvc
services.description: Manages telephony state on devices with cellular voice modems.
services.impact: None on desktop PCs and standard Wi-Fi laptops (Phone Link uses a separate app process).

services.name: lfsvc
services.description: Monitors the current geographic location of the system and manages geofences.
services.impact: Weather widgets or apps using automatic Windows GPS location will ask for a manual city/zip code.

services.name: TrkWks
services.description: Maintains links between NTFS files across computers in an enterprise Windows domain.
services.impact: None for home users; saves constant background NTFS tracking overhead.

services.name: WMPNetworkSvc
services.displayName: Windows Media Player Network Sharing Service
services.description: Shares legacy Windows Media Player libraries to other networked DLNA devices.
services.impact: None unless you stream via legacy Windows Media Player DLNA.

services.name: icssvc
services.description: Provides the ability to share a cellular or Ethernet connection as a Wi-Fi hotspot.
services.impact: You cannot turn your PC into a Wi-Fi Mobile Hotspot while disabled.

services.name: Spooler
services.description: Spools print jobs and handles interaction with physical and PDF virtual printers. Often consumes 15-40 MB RAM continuously.
services.impact: You will not be able to print to physical printers or 'Microsoft Print to PDF' while stopped.

services.name: PrintNotify
services.description: Opens custom printer dialogs and manages printer notifications.
services.impact: Safe to disable if you do not use a printer.

services.name: stisvc
services.description: Provides image acquisition services for flatbed scanners and some legacy cameras.
services.impact: Document scanners won't work while disabled (standard USB webcams still work normally).

services.name: bthserv
services.description: Supports discovery and association of remote Bluetooth devices.
services.impact: Bluetooth headphones, mice, and controllers will not connect. Safe if your desktop has no Bluetooth or you only use wired/2.4GHz dongle gear.

services.name: BTAGService
services.description: Supports the audio gateway role of the Bluetooth Handsfree Profile.
services.impact: Bluetooth headsets won't transmit audio if disabled.

services.name: SysMain
services.description: Preloads frequently used apps into RAM. Can consume 50-150 MB RAM and cause high disk I/O spikes.
services.impact: On fast NVMe SSDs, disabling frees RAM and background CPU/disk spikes with negligible app launch difference.

services.name: WSearch
services.description: Continuously indexes files, emails, and content in the background (often uses 40-120 MB RAM + disk usage).
services.impact: Start menu app search still works, but instant content search inside documents/files will be slower (great to disable if you use Everything by voidtools).

services.name: XblAuthManager
services.description: Provides authentication and authorization services for interacting with Xbox Live.
services.impact: Safe to disable if you only use Steam/Epic and never play Xbox Game Pass or Microsoft Store games.

services.name: XblGameSave
services.description: Syncs cloud save data for Xbox Game Pass and Xbox Play Anywhere titles.
services.impact: Safe to disable if you don't play Xbox Game Pass titles.

services.name: XboxNetApiSvc
services.description: Supports peer-to-peer multiplayer networking for Xbox Live games.
services.impact: Safe to disable if you don't play Xbox Live multiplayer games.

services.name: XboxGipSvc
services.description: Manages Xbox Wireless Adapter accessories.
services.impact: Safe to disable if you don't use an official Xbox controller.

services.name: WbioSrvc
services.description: Captures, compares, and stores fingerprint and Windows Hello facial biometric data.
services.impact: Safe to disable on desktops without a fingerprint reader or Windows Hello IR camera.

services.name: SCardSvr
services.description: Manages access to physical smart card readers for enterprise login cards.
services.impact: None unless you log in with a physical enterprise/government Smart Card.

services.name: TabletInputService
services.displayName: Touch Keyboard and Handwriting Panel Service
services.description: Enables touch keyboard and stylus handwriting on touchscreen devices.
services.impact: Note: In Windows 11, disabling this may also disable the Win + . (period) Emoji picker.

services.name: SensorService
services.description: Manages ambient light sensors, accelerometers, and auto-rotation on tablets.
services.impact: None on desktop PCs or standard laptops without auto-brightness/auto-rotate sensors.

services.name: SensrSvc
services.description: Monitors ambient light and orientation sensors to adjust screen brightness and rotation.
services.impact: None on desktops.

services.name: SensorDataService
services.description: Delivers data from various tablet/convertible hardware sensors.
services.impact: None on desktops and non-convertible laptops.

services.name: hvhost
services.description: Provides an interface for the Hyper-V hypervisor to provide per-partition counters to the host OS.
services.impact: Safe to disable if you do not use Hyper-V, WSL2, or Docker Desktop.

services.name: vmickvpexchange
services.description: Provides a mechanism to exchange metadata between a Hyper-V virtual machine and the host.
services.impact: Safe to disable on bare-metal PCs not running Hyper-V.

services.name: vmicguestinterface
services.description: Provides an interface for the Hyper-V host to copy files to or from the virtual machine.
services.impact: Safe to disable on bare-metal PCs not running Hyper-V.

services.name: vmicshutdown
services.description: Provides a mechanism to shut down a guest virtual machine from the host.
services.impact: Safe to disable on bare-metal PCs.

services.name: vmicheartbeat
services.description: Monitors the state of a virtual machine by reporting a heartbeat at regular intervals.
services.impact: Safe to disable on bare-metal PCs.

services.name: vmicvmsession
services.description: Provides a mechanism to manage virtual machines with PowerShell without networking.
services.impact: Safe to disable on bare-metal PCs.

services.name: vmicrdv
services.description: Provides a platform for communication between the virtual machine and the host.
services.impact: Safe to disable on bare-metal PCs.

services.name: vmictimesync
services.description: Synchronizes the system time of a virtual machine with the system time of the physical computer.
services.impact: Safe to disable on bare-metal PCs.

services.name: vmicvss
services.description: Coordinates the communications required to use Volume Shadow Copy Service to back up a virtual machine.
services.impact: Safe to disable on bare-metal PCs.

startupPatterns.reason: Stops OneDrive from syncing cloud files automatically on boot (~60-150 MB RAM). Files won't sync until you open OneDrive.
Stops Microsoft Edge from pre-loading in the background on boot. Edge will still work and update normally when opened.
Stops Adobe Creative Cloud background updaters and telemetry daemons. Adobe apps still launch normally when clicked.
Stops Google's background updater/crash daemon from running at login (Chrome still updates automatically when opened).
Stops Spotify from auto-opening on login (~150-300 MB RAM). You can launch Spotify manually whenever you want music.
Stops Discord from auto-launching on boot (~200-400 MB RAM). You won't receive desktop notifications until you open Discord.
Stops Steam client from auto-starting on boot (~150-300 MB RAM). Games won't auto-update until you open Steam.
Stops Epic Games Launcher from auto-starting on boot (~200-350 MB RAM). Launch manually when playing Epic games.
Stops Microsoft Teams from auto-starting on login (~250-500 MB RAM). You won't get chat/call alerts until you open Teams.
Disables legacy Cortana voice assistant startup entry. Zero impact on Windows 10/11.
Stops Skype from running in the system tray on boot. Launch manually when needed.
Stops Brave Browser's background updater scheduled task. Brave updates automatically when you open the browser.
Stops Opera Browser's background updater task. Opera still updates when opened.
Stops Firefox background silent updater task. Firefox updates normally when launched.
Realtek Audio Universal Service / Tray panel. Disabling may stop headphone jack pop-up detection or audio effects panel.
Intel Graphics tray/hotkey helper or telemetry task. Display driver still works; display hotkeys (Ctrl+Alt+Arrow) won't trigger.
NVIDIA GeForce Experience / Telemetry background updater task. GPU drivers still work; automatic game profile updates pause.
AMD Radeon Software tray and background updater. GPU driver works normally without the startup tray UI.
Stops Zoom from running in the background on boot. Zoom will still open normally whenever you click a meeting link.
Stops Slack from auto-starting on boot (~250-450 MB RAM). You won't receive Slack desktop notifications until opened.
Stops Docker Desktop from starting a Linux VM on every boot (~1-2 GB RAM!). Launch Docker manually when coding.
Stops Dropbox background file sync and updater on boot. Files sync only when Dropbox is launched.
Apple background helper for automatic iPhone/iPad USB detection or iCloud sync.
ASUS OEM background updater/RGB/telemetry task. Disabling stops background ASUS update checks (fan/RGB presets stay applied).
HP OEM support/telemetry background task. Safe to disable to save background CPU and RAM.
Dell OEM SupportAssist / automatic updater task. Safe to disable; you can check for Dell driver updates manually.
Lenovo Vantage OEM background updater/telemetry task. Safe to disable unless you use Lenovo battery charge thresholds.
Razer Synapse RGB & macro background suite (~150-300 MB RAM). Custom mouse macros/RGB lighting require it running.
Logitech G HUB / Options+ custom mouse button & DPI daemon. Custom mouse button mappings won't apply while stopped.
Brother Printer status monitor and software update checker. Safe to disable unless you actively use a Brother printer/scanner.
Graphics drawing tablet pen pressure & shortcut driver. Safe to disable when your drawing tablet is unplugged.
Third-party cleaner or nagware background updater task that runs on boot. Safe to disable.
